title: Cortical Degradation Analysis with ABBA
author: Joseph Martin
materials: Order images from rostral to caudal
QuPath Start-Up and Image Import"), proceed to "
Double-click on the number listed for "Pixel width"
Adjust X Rotation for dorsal-ventral asymmetry
Adjust Y Rotation for left-right asymmetry
In the ABBA window, select all slices.

steps.title: Set and check Fiji wrappers
steps.instruction: Open Fiji, run the “set and check” wrapper, and specify the full paths to elastix.exe and transformix.exe (e.g., C:\elastix-5.0.1-win64\elastix.exe and C:\elastix-5.0.1-win64\transformix.exe).

steps.title: Acquire and crop scanner images
steps.instruction: Using the Keyence BZX‑10 (2X objective), download stitched images, crop each stitched image so it contains only one tissue section, and place the cropped images into a PowerPoint named with the cohort number (one slide per image).

substeps.instruction: Use PowerPoint’s crop tool on each slide.
Save each cropped image as a .TIF file in a folder called “Cropped”.
Name files as #Cohort_Genotype_Condition_Stain_1.1.1 where the suffix 1.1.1 denotes slide 1, row 1, tissue 1 (right‑to‑left order).

steps.title: Order images rostral‑caudal
steps.instruction: Arrange the .TIF files from rostral to caudal, duplicate the “Cropped” folder, create a new folder named “Ordered”, and move the images into “Ordered” adding a leading order number (e.g., 05#Cohort_Genotype_Condition_Stain_1.1.1).

substeps.instruction: Verify orientation of each image.
Have a second person check the ordered folder and the original PowerPoint for comparison.
Confirm that all filenames are final before proceeding to QuPath.

steps.title: Create QuPath folder hierarchy
steps.instruction: Within the lab file system create three tiered folders:

substeps.instruction: Tier 1: Cohort ID.
Tier 2: Conditions (e.g., A.WT, B.Het, A.SurWT, B.SurHet, etc.).
Tier 3 (inside each condition):
A. Ordered
B. QuPath and ABBA Projects
C. For Post‑ABBA Analysis.

steps.title: Set up QuPath project
steps.instruction: Open QuPath, drag the “B. QuPath and ABBA Projects” folder into the left sidebar, confirm creation of a new project when prompted.

steps.title: Import ordered images
steps.instruction: Open the “A. Ordered” folder, select all images (Ctrl + A, click first image first), drag them into the QuPath sidebar, and complete the import window steps 7‑9 before clicking “Import”.

substeps.instruction: Select “Bio‑Formats builder” as Image server.
Set Image type to “Fluorescence”.
Ensure “Auto‑generate pyramids” is unchecked.

steps.title: Set pixel size to 5 µm
steps.instruction: For one imported image, double‑click its name, open the “Image” tab, double‑click the “Pixel width” value, change both pixel width and pixel height to 5 µm, and click OK.

substeps.instruction: Open the “Workflow” tab, click “Create Script”.
Run the script for the whole project (Run → Run for project → >> → OK).
Verify that a second image also shows 5 µm pixel width/height.
Save the project (File → Save) and close QuPath.

steps.title: Open ABBA in Fiji
steps.instruction: In Fiji/ImageJ, search for “abba”, select “ABBA – ABBA Start”, click “Start”, choose the Allen Brain Atlas V3p1, and select “coronal” slicing mode.

substeps.instruction: Familiarize with mouse controls: left‑click drag, wheel zoom, right‑click pan, up/down keys zoom.
Atlas channels: 0 = Nissl, 1 = Auto‑fluorescence, 2 = Region borders.
Adjust slice spacing with the “displayed slicing [microns]” slider (10 steps = 100 µm, 50 steps = 500 µm).
Use Positioning Mode for initial placement; Review Mode for single‑slice review.

steps.title: Import QuPath project into ABBA
steps.instruction: In ABBA choose Import → Import QuPath Project, select the project.qpproj file from the “B. QuPath and ABBA Projects” folder, set initial AP position to 4, set spacing increment to 0.08 mm (80 µm), accept default BDV dataset options, select all slices (Shift‑click or rectangle), and click the “Vis.” and “Ch_0” headings to display all slices.

steps.title: Interactive tissue alignment
steps.instruction: In Review Mode, drag each tissue left/right to roughly match the atlas, adjust X and Y rotation using the Atlas Slicing controls to align hippocampal asymmetry, then click “Align – Interactive Transform” to fine‑tune rotation, X/Y scale, and X/Y translation for each slice.

substeps.instruction: Save the mapping state as “State-1_Interactive-Transformation-Complete”.

steps.title: Enable atlas map channel
steps.instruction: Turn on channel 2 (atlas map) and turn off channels 0 and 1, then select all tissues (click first image in the image‑set table, Ctrl + A).

steps.title: Affine registration
steps.instruction: Run Affine Registration using the following parameters:

substeps.instruction: Atlas channel: 2 only.
Slices channel: whichever channel shows the slices (0 or 1).
Registration re‑sampling: 15 µm.
Background offset value: 0.
Do NOT check “Show registration results as ImagePlus”.

steps.title: Save affine registration state
steps.instruction: After registration completes (green circles turn green), save the project state as “State-2_Affine-Registration-Complete”.

steps.title: Spline registration
steps.instruction: Run Spline Registration with these parameters:

substeps.instruction: Atlas channel: 2 only.
Slices channel: whichever channel shows the slices (0 or 1).
Number of control points along X (minimum 2): 30.
Registration re‑sampling: 15 µm.
Background offset value: 0.
Do NOT check “Show registration results as ImagePlus”.

steps.title: Save spline registration state
steps.instruction: When spline registration finishes, save the project state as “State-3_Spline-Registration-Complete”.

steps.title: Prepare post‑ABBA file sets
steps.instruction: Copy ordered images to the “C. For Post‑ABBA Analysis” folder and create a subfolder for each image:

substeps.instruction: In the cohort folder, open the condition just mapped.
In “A. Ordered”, select the first image, Ctrl + A, Ctrl + C (exclude any .BFMEMO files).
Paste into “C. For Post‑ABBA Analysis”.
For each image, copy its filename, create a new folder (Shift + Ctrl + N) named exactly that filename, and move the corresponding ROIset.zip into that folder.
Also move the .TIF image into the same subfolder.

steps.title: Sort and prune ROIs in Fiji
steps.instruction: For each image:

substeps.instruction: Open Fiji, drag the .TIF image into Fiji.
Rename the ROI zip folder by appending “_RoiSet-Complete”.
Drag the renamed ROI set into Fiji; the ROI Manager opens.
Click More → Sort to alphabetically sort ROIs (by hemisphere).
Delete all ROIs not needed (see list of ROIs to keep).
Select the first ROI, shift‑click the ROI just before the first desired ROI (e.g., “MO”), delete the highlighted block.
Repeat until only the desired ROIs remain.
Ensure no ROI is selected (click a random ROI then “Deselect”).
Save the ROI set as “RoiSet‑Isocortex‑<Initials>”.

steps.title: Split ROIs into hemispheres
steps.instruction: For each kept ROI set:

substeps.instruction: In the ROI Manager, select the first ROI, click More → Split.
Rename the resulting left‑hemisphere ROI as “LH <Region>” and the right‑hemisphere ROI as “RH <Region>”.
Delete all small polygon ROIs generated by the split and delete the combined hemisphere ROI.
Repeat for all regions and all images.
Click More → Sort to alphabetically sort hemispheric ROIs.
Deselect any ROI (click random ROI → Deselect).
Save the final set as “RoiSet‑Isocortex‑<Initials>‑Final”.

steps.title: Identify degraded images
steps.instruction: Review the images in the “Ordered” folder, compare each ChABC‑treated image with its corresponding biPen control, and note any tissue where PNNs appear dimmer.

substeps.instruction: Record the image order number for each degraded image.
Create a new spreadsheet (Degradation Analysis Spreadsheet.xlsx) named with the cohort number.
Rename the sheet “Cohort #” to the actual cohort number.
Fill cells A4‑D4 with cohort metadata and E4‑I4 with additional info.
Add a row for each hemisphere (left and right) of each degraded image, entering columns E‑I as described (order number, section number, etc.).

steps.title: Measure total ROI area
steps.instruction: For each degraded image:

substeps.instruction: Open the image in Fiji, remove any existing scale (Analyze → Set Scale → Click to Remove Scale, check “Global”, OK).
When opening subsequent images, uncheck “Disable Global Calibration” and check “Disable these Messages”.
Drag the corresponding “RoiSet‑Isocortex‑<Initials>‑Final” file into Fiji, click “Show All”.
Using the polygon tool, outline the portion of each ROI where PNNs are dimmer, close the polygon, press “T” to add it to the ROI Manager, rename it “(L/R)H‑ROI_reduced”.
Save this reduced ROI as “RoiSet‑Isocortex‑<Initials>‑Analyzed”.
Select the original full ROI (e.g., “LH_SSp‑bfd”), click “Measure”, and record the “Full Area” value in the spreadsheet.

steps.title: Measure depleted ROI area
steps.instruction: Continuing for the same image:

substeps.instruction: Select the reduced ROI (“(L/R)H‑ROI_reduced”) in the ROI Manager, click “Measure”, and record the “Depleted Area” value in the spreadsheet.
If multiple ROIs are reduced, repeat the outlining and measurement for each.

steps.title: Record rostral‑caudal coordinate
steps.instruction: For each reduced ROI:

substeps.instruction: Load the saved ABBA state for the cohort (the .ABBA file in “B. QuPath and ABBA Projects”).
Enter Review Mode, navigate to the tissue of interest, choose Display → Show mouse atlas position.
Hover over the centre of the reduced ROI and record the first of the three coordinates (rostral‑caudal axis) in the spreadsheet column “(ROI) Map”.
Repeat for all reduced ROIs.

steps.title: Calculate percentage depletion
steps.instruction: In the analysis spreadsheet:

substeps.instruction: For each ROI, enter the formula = (Depleted Area cell) / (Full Area cell) (e.g., =(Z16/J16)).
Copy the formula down the column for all ROIs.
Select the entire “% Depleted” column and change the number format to “Percentage”.
Save the spreadsheet and back‑up all files to the server.
